description:
Guest checkout + optional accounts, ticket wallet, the identity substrate for transfers, resale and purchase limits.

**Conditions of Success:**
- Guest can buy with email only; account creation optional and retroactively claims guest orders
- Account wallet lists tickets, passes, lodging and wristbands
- Identity model supports per-customer purchase limits (TKT-20) and transfers (TKT-9)

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

**Amended (grilling):** strict-limit events can require an account to purchase (TKT-20); the accounts model must support per-event login requirements without breaking the guest-first default.

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.
Backlog grilling 2026-07-12 (owner decisions): account-required-for-limited-events lands on the accounts model.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
### Decomposition - TKT-21 into four vertical slices

Run mode: **fully autonomous, gateless** (owner waiver, 2026-08-06). Backend: local tracker.

Guest checkout already exists end to end, so the epic's real gap is that a **customer** does not
exist anywhere in the system. Four slices, each end-to-end and demoable on its own:

| Ticket | Slice | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| TKT-220 | US-A1 - customer accounts: register, sign in, sign out (+ the placement ADR) | - |
| TKT-221 | US-A2 - a signed-in purchase is attributed to the account | TKT-220 |
| TKT-222 | US-A3 - the wallet: my orders, linking to the existing ticket page | TKT-221 |
| TKT-223 | US-A4 - claim a past guest order into the account | TKT-222 |

Cycle check: the dependency graph is a straight line, no cycle.

**What already exists and is deliberately not rebuilt:** `buyer_pii` (name + email) and
`orders.guest_order_ref` in commerce; the guest ticket-retrieval page
`web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef].astro`; the whole staff-auth stack
(catalog `staff_accounts` migration 0015 + `web/backoffice/src/lib/session.ts`/`gate.ts`) which is
the design precedent these tickets mirror, ADR-042.

**Not decomposed into a ticket, on purpose:** the "identity model supports per-customer purchase
limits and transfers" COS. That is satisfied by TKT-221 giving orders a stable customer reference -
the limits themselves are TKT-20 and transfers are TKT-9/TKT-160, both separate epics. Building
limit machinery here would be building for a ticket that has not been shaped.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Implementation readiness - CONCERNS

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | OK | `make check` on every child; the browser-submit gate on all four (every one adds a form) |
| Vertical slices | OK | Each child crosses migration -> service -> contract -> storefront and is demoable alone |
| Sized to one reviewable PR | WARN | TKT-220 is the fattest (table + 2 operations + session module + 3 forms + an ADR). It is not splittable without leaving a non-demoable half - an accounts table nobody can sign in to |
| Prefactoring split out first | OK | None needed: the staff-auth stack is the seam and it already exists |
| Ordered by dependency | OK | Straight line, no forward dependency, cycle check passed |
| AC verifiable | OK | No "works correctly"; the soft ACs are written as *"the plan states X and why"*, which is checkable |
| Children linked | OK | 220 <- 221 <- 222 <- 223 |
| Context-memo baked | OK | Per child, incl. the credential blast-radius entries decomposition.md requires for auth tickets |
| No unvalidated assumption | WARN | See concern 1 |

**Concerns:**

1. **(TKT-220) Where customer identity lives is not decided, and it is the load-bearing choice.**
   ADR-042 put staff in catalog *because catalog owns organizers and staff administer an organizer*.
   A customer administers nothing, so that reasoning does not transplant - it has to be re-run, and
   ADR-042 has already rejected the two escape hatches (a sixth service, the gateway). The child
   carries this as an ADR acceptance criterion rather than an assumption, so it is decided in the
   open at plan time. It is a concern and not a FAIL because every option is inside the existing
   five-service cut.

2. **(TKT-222) The epic's COS-2 is knowingly narrowed.** "Wallet lists tickets, passes, lodging and
   wristbands" - passes (TKT-12), lodging (TKT-13) and wristbands (TKT-15) are un-started Backlog
   epics with no schema anywhere. The wallet will list orders and tickets. The epic's COS-2 is
   therefore **not** fully met by this run and should not be marked as such.

3. **(TKT-220) The public sign-in surface will ship unrate-limited.** TKT-195 exists for the
   back-office form and is still open; a storefront registration/sign-in endpoint is a *more*
   exposed version of the same problem. TKT-220's non-goals require it to **file** the follow-up
   rather than solve it - flagged here so the omission is a recorded decision, not a gap.

4. **The whole epic is an auth change by construction** (credentials, password hashing, sessions,
   cookies, an authorization boundary on a read) and TKT-221/223 add data migrations to the
   **checkout path**. Both are named in the owner's stop conditions - they are *anticipated by the
   tickets*, so this run proceeds, but every plan and every review pass on these four should be read
   with that in mind.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS - proceedable. Nothing is structurally broken; concerns 1-3 are decisions
deferred to plan time on purpose, and concern 4 is a property of the epic rather than a defect in
the decomposition.

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
### Epic closeout — TKT-21, run gateless

All four children are **Done** and merged. This ran under the owner's waiver of all four human gates,
recorded in full on TKT-220's claim comment.

| Child | Shipped | PR | Diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TKT-220** US-A1 — accounts: register, sign in, sign out | ADR-049 · `customer_accounts` · storefront session | [#178](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/178) | +4,205/−28 |
| **TKT-221** US-A2 — a signed-in purchase belongs to the account | signed customer assertion · `/checkout` bridge · `orders.customer_id` | [#179](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/179) | +1,539/−82 |
| **TKT-222** US-A3 — the wallet | scoped read + index + plan proof · catalog display names | [#180](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/180) | +2,326/−11 |
| **TKT-223** US-A4 — claim a past guest order | one conditional UPDATE · the invariant's one exception | [#181](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/181) | +1,473/−11 |

**Total ≈ +9,540 / −132 across 104 file-changes, ~5h20m Ready→Done, 0 minutes of human wait.**

### The COS, honestly

1. *Guest buys with email only; account optional and retroactively claims guest orders* — ✅ **met**.
2. *Wallet lists tickets, passes, lodging and wristbands* — ⚠️ **narrowed at decomposition and still
   narrowed**: passes (TKT-12), lodging (TKT-13) and wristbands (TKT-15) are un-started epics with no
   schema anywhere. The wallet lists orders and their tickets. **This COS is not met and should not be
   marked so.**
3. *Identity model supports per-customer limits (TKT-20) and transfers (TKT-9)* — ✅ **substrate met**:
   a stable, indexed, immutable-except-by-claim `orders.customer_id`.

### What the gateless run cost, in one place

Five recorded `overrides:` across the four tickets. Two are `[high]`, and both are the same shape —
**a reviewer rediscovering a trade-off an ADR already records**:

- **TKT-220** — registration answers 409 on a duplicate: an unauthenticated membership oracle over the
  whole customer base. Raised `[high]` in all three passes, overridden three times. → **TKT-224**.
- **TKT-223** — a leaked order reference permits permanent, irreversible takeover of someone's order.
  → **TKT-225** filed, **TKT-202** annotated as its prerequisite.

Plus three narrowings where a claim was corrected rather than the code: the SSR body deadline, the
source scanner's reach, and refusal timing.

**Those five paragraphs are the part of this run a human cannot reconstruct from the merged diffs**,
and they are the argument for reading closeouts rather than commits.

### Follow-ups this epic filed

**TKT-224** (rate-limit the public customer auth surface) · **TKT-225** (operator un-claim path) ·
**TKT-202** annotated. All three unshaped and in Backlog; `Backlog → Ready` stays a human transition.

### The dominant defect class, measured

**Eight tests that could not fail**, across four tickets. None was found by writing the test
carefully; every one was found by mutation-checking or an adversarial pass. The remedy was identical
each time — *make the test call what production calls* — and it is now written down
([three ways one test could not fail](docs/learnings/2026-08-06-three-ways-one-test-could-not-fail.md),
postscript).

**Three driver-level defects** in TKT-222 reached a green `make check` and were found only by driving
a real browser
([a fake store cannot see the driver](docs/learnings/2026-08-06-a-fake-store-cannot-see-the-driver.md)).

Four learnings promoted in total; the fourth is
[a guard's worst failure is not seeing](docs/learnings/2026-08-06-a-guards-worst-failure-is-not-seeing.md).

### The one process change worth the owner's attention

**TKT-196** — the browser-submit harness. Four tickets, four hand-rolled Playwright scripts plus a
catalog seeder, all in a scratch directory that dies with this session. It is not ceremonial: it
caught guest checkout 403ing behind a new bridge, three driver-level SQL defects, and the entire
epic's end-to-end flow. It will be rewritten from scratch by whoever touches this next.
